utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge regarding the participation in combat operations of the so-called assault battalion, or the intervention battalion, at the time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: On one occasion when the positions of my unit were attacked, they came to assist us to defend the positions that we held. I remember that they came, that there were some people who came from some intervention unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was there digging of trenches on the part of the front line where you were?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Of course, there were trenches that were being dug. Every soldier who didn't dig a trench was at risk of being killed or wounded. Where would a soldier hide if not in a trench?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you personally dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your comrades, your fellow soldiers, did they also dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Of course. Everybody dug trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Where you were at that position, did civilians come to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that, not where I was in my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know about another position where this was happening?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I know that civilians were making bunkers and enforced positions on the embankment near the Sava River. That's what I could see from the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In October 1992, where were you transferred, or rather, where did you start working?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I started working on a work obligation, in a hospital, working in microbiology, and soon after that I went to Belgrade and I continued to study medicine, because, as I told you, I was about to graduate in medical studies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: While you were working in the hospital, Dr. Pivasevic, was there any medical personnel, or was there medical personnel of all three nationalities, of all three ethnicities? And if there were, who can you remember? Can you just give us some names?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: The answer is yes, there were. But bringing people who were wounded on the line, bringing to hospital, I met other people, my colleagues, Dr. Rusmir Jusufovic; Dr. Mesud Nogic, who was in fact, I think, a director of the medical centre; there was Dr. Ruza, a female doctor, who was a paediatrist [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name of the last doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't manage to catch the very last name. Did you say Dr. Harcinovic?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Damir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. All of these colleagues, they are Muslims and Croats; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You told me -- you asked me about other ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Dr. Stevic; is that correct? Did I hear you well?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Mladen Stevic. He's a Serb. He also worked there at the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What else do you know about Dr. Stevic? Did he only give medical assistance in the hospital or did you go outside of the hospital and offer medical assistance?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: On one occasion when I brought a wounded person, Mladen wasn't around, I asked, because it was customary at the time, that everybody should be at their places of employment and I asked what happened to Mladen and they told me he had gone to a secondary school centre to examine some people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And who was at the secondary school centre?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic. I'm just wondering: In terms of the summary of what we were anticipating with Dr. Pivasevic, it was variant A and B, in other words, P3, and/or the structure of the SDS. That's what you informed us. I'm just wondering why we're hearing from this witness about digging trenches and the composition of the medical centre, which we've already heard quite a bit about already.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm ready to go to another topic, but, as I said, I provided weeks ago to my learned friend a summary of topics, and then it was a more detailed version of proofing notes that I provided yesterday. So all these topics I believe are included. Maybe I can hear from my learned friend. But I don't have any problem to go to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on the outline, it looks like we're coming to the end. So I have no objection, as long as we're getting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. I was about to say: Fine, Mr. Pantelic, if that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Dr. Pivasevic, the previous question was: And who were these people who were at the secondary school centre? Can you tell us: What kind of people were there?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: At that time, I heard that there were people who were imprisoned, who had been armed, in whose houses police had found weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what is their ethnicity? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me: In the course of 1992, SDS, as a party, did they carry out their function? What do you know about it? I mean, were there any party activities?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No. There was a freeze on the activity of all the political parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On the basis of which decision was the activity of all political parties frozen? Was this a municipal decision or was this a decision that came from a higher level?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I have no information regarding this. I only know that at that time, in the beginning, and in the course of 1992, I know that the party activity was non-existent; it wasn't functioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, Dr. Pivasevic: Do you have any personal knowledge whether Dr. Blagoje Simic, during the period before middle of April of 1992, was he involved in sending some young men to training, to military training, somewhere in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No, I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At the meetings of the Municipal Board of the SDS, was the topic of sending young men or young candidates for military equipment [as interpreted] discussed?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No, not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: His previous answer, they asked him whether Blagoje Simic was involved in sending some young men to training. He said: I have no knowledge of that. Does he mean he doesn't know whether or not he did it or that he did not do that? It's vague, the answer. He could be meaning that: I have no knowledge of him ever sending it because he didn't do it, or is he saying: I don't know anything about this topic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure the witness can clarify his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The answer is no. No, I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, Dr. Pivasevic, whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Sorry. Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic, but the answer of the witness is exactly the same as the one that Mr. Weiner was seeking clarification of, in that he says: "No, I have no knowledge of that." Could you perhaps, with the witness, clarify as to the way Mr. Weiner perhaps suggested?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Meaning he has no knowledge of people being -- he has no knowledge of the topic or that Simic -- the defendant Simic did not do something?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Dr. Pivasevic, it's very simple: As far as you know, did Dr. Blagoje Simic send young men from the territory of the municipality of Samac to military training in Serbia? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next question: Do you have any knowledge whether, from the municipality of Samac, some young men went to military training in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Next question: On the level of the SDS Municipal Board of Samac, was it ever discussed or established a party armed unit of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The level of the Municipal Board of the Samac SDS, was ever an option discussed of bringing volunteers from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, according to your personal knowledge: Did Dr. Blagoje Simic, in party contacts, as well as in informal contacts, ever speak in favour of ethnic discrimination in Samac?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear from anyone in Samac, from your environment, that somebody was talking about Dr. Blagoje Simic as being a propogandist for ethnic discrimination in Samac?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the end, Dr. Pivasevic, can you tell us: What was the method of work of Dr. Simic at these meetings, party meetings and contacts with people? Do you have any personal knowledge? Can you tell the Trial Chamber about that? What was his behaviour? What was the way he spoke to people and had contacts with people?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I was able to know, Dr. Simic, he was always tolerant, he was always finding the right -- he was balancing between the people, if you can understand what I'm saying. And in the pre-electoral campaign, when we were discussing and deciding who were the people who would be heading certain lists and who would be included in certain lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Dr. Pivasevic, in the political programme of the SDS, in their manifesto, is there anywhere a topic which is related dealing with ethnic discrimination or annulment of human rights of other nations or other nationalities?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: The answer is no. Among other things, the programme, the manifesto of the SDS was public. It was in all the media. It could be found in written form, electronic form. And the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Which party -- to which party belongs the joint representative of the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borislav Parov, a member of the SDS party.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I've finished with the examination of this witness. [Interpretation] And now the Prosecutor will cross-examine you, Dr. Pivasevic, and perhaps later on I will ask some more questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Unless Defence counsel have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I may ask. No. They don't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Doctor. My name is Phillip Weiner. I'm a Prosecutor with the Office of the Prosecutor here, and I'm going to be asking you some questions. Now, about an hour ago you mentioned that you became a member of the SDS party, which was initially established by a Jovan Raskovic. You described as a Gandhi-like figure. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that just before his death, in the spring/early summer of 1992, Mr. Raskovic made the following statements about the SDS party: "I am responsible for the preparations of this war, even if these weren't military preparations. If I hadn't caused these emotional tensions in the Serbian people, it wouldn't have happened. My party and I have inflamed Serbian nationalism, not only in Croatia but also all over Bosnia-Herzegovina. Without our influence, it wouldn't have been possible for the Serbian Democratic Party or for Mr. Karadzic to come to power in Bosnia-Herzegovina. We have pushed this thing and have given it an identity. I have repeated again and again to these people that it's something that comes from heaven, not from earth." Were you aware that the founder of your SDS party made this statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No. I have not read that statement of Dr. Raskovic. But I did say that his methods were Gandhi-like because he always sat down, he always wanted to listen, to discuss, and he initiated lots of meetings with Franjo Tudjman in Zagreb. And as you know, with the arrival of the HDZ, the Serbs were outvoted and expelled as a constitutive member. And because of his ways and the way he wanted to discuss, I mentioned that he was a Gandhi-like figure because he was always promoting peace and solutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in that statement, he indicated his dismay with Dr. Radovan Karadzic, who he used to describe as his protege; isn't that correct? Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, as I said, I have not read that statement made by Dr. Raskovic. However, Dr. Raskovic was a psychiatrist and he knew how to give interviews, and very often his interviews were very intellectual. I cannot interpret this statement in a way you read it to me. I would have to read the whole interview in order for me to give you any answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue on. You testified that you were a founding member of the SDS in Samac, or in that founding steering committee, and that you've remained in the party some approximately 13 years now?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Sometime in the month of July 1990, several hundred people got together in Slatina --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, no, no?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: -- and they formed --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You've been in the SDS for approximately 13 years now. You've remained in the party, 12 years, 13 years, in that range?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: From 1992 -- in 1992, the work of the party was frozen. In 1993, I was -- I joined university. In 1994, when I graduated, I spent a few months in Brcko and I was an intern there. And after that, I was mobilised in the army. I was not active in the SDS up until the spring of 1996, after the Dayton Peace Accord and after the end of the war I got involved again in politics, and after the multiparty elections I was elected.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You've remained, sir, in the party even though three of its key leaders or its three key leaders have all been indicted by the court here for genocide; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Maybe it might be a bit confusing to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a member of parliament, a doctor. He can answer simple questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. Just a moment, my learned friend. I'm not objecting to your -- the subject of your question. No. Please. First of all, it's too vague. What does it mean, three key figures, three key leaders, sorry? Do we have a name? And then I believe that this Tribunal cannot indict anyone. It can be only Office of the Prosecutor. So let's be precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure there's no objection to giving the witness the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Biljana Plavsic, Momcilo Krajisnik, and Radovan Karadzic have all been indicted for genocide, the three key leaders of the SDS. You've remained in that party even though its three key leaders have been indicted; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Is everything okay with the interpretation, with the headphones?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can you hear?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you. Yes, yes, yes. Very well. I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you have remained in the party even though the three key leaders of the SDS, Biljana Plavsic, Momcilo Krajisnik, and Radovan Karadzic, have all been indicted for genocide; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: They were indicted, but they were not found guilty, as far as I know. And it's a very large party. After the elections, it won almost 200,000 votes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware that one of the three key leaders of the SDS party, Biljana Plavsic, has pled guilty to the crime of persecution in this courthouse?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Maybe we could establish, first of all, whether, at the time of the indictment, when the indictment was issued, Biljana Plavsic was a member of SDS. Maybe that should be your first question, to establish the knowledge of this witness with that regard. Or maybe my learned friend can rephrase the question, saying: Well, at the time -- well, he was indicted I don't know in which year, but on that time he was -- 1992 or 1993, she was a top leader of SDS, in this relation. Because otherwise it's too large, too general, too vague, I believe. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic is referring to the period of the indictment that is end of 1991 up to end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that one of the key leaders of the SDS party, the president or the key leader of the SDS party, from 1990 to 1992, Biljana Plavsic, has pled guilty in this court that during that time period, during the war period, that she committed persecution against the non-Serb community? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know -- can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, Mrs. Plavsic was a member of the presidency, and she was a candidate for the SDS. I also know that Mrs. Plavsic pled guilty before this Tribunal, but that is her own affair. It is her own decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, were you aware that Mrs. Plavsic has admitted that she and other SDS leaders orchestrated a policy of persecution against the non-Serbian population of Bosnia, and she did that during 1991 and 1992? Were you aware of that, that she has admitted that?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: From the media, I found out that Mrs. Plavsic pled some sort of guiltiness or I don't know really to what she pled guilty, because I work a lot and I wasn't able to follow everything, but I know that she got 10 to 11 years of imprisonment for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, we'll get back to Mrs. Plavsic in a minute. You joined the SDS and you've remained in the SDS apparently because you've agreed in its policies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I joined the SDS at the very beginning, when the party was formed in 1990. Then Mrs. Plavsic was candidated as a member of the presidency. She was a woman who was a professor. She came from a very well-known Serbian family. And it is quite normal that everywhere in the world, people who are such -- so highly educated and come from such good families, candidate themselves at such positions. The SDS promoted peaceful solutions, and a peaceful living of the three constitutive peoples of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Muslims, Croats, and Serbs. And the SDS never promoted in its programme and it never had as its goal to promote a discriminatory or genocidal politick.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that it was a policy of the SDS to enforce ethnic separation by force? Were you aware of that, sir, that that was a policy in 1991 and 1992 in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of that, that anybody talked about any force.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit P164, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to direct your attention to paragraphs 10 and 11. Now, paragraph 10, Biljana Plavsic, one of the three major leaders of the SDS at the time, states: "The SDS, in paragraph 10, and the Bosnian Serb leadership, were committed to a primary goal that all Serbs in the former Yugoslavia would remain in a common state. One method of achieving this goal was by separating the ethnic communities in BH. By October 1991, the Bosnian Serb leadership, including Mrs. Plavsic, knew and intended that the separation of the ethnic communities would include the permanent removal of ethnic populations, either by agreement or by force, and further knew that any forcible removal of non-Serbs from Serbian-claimed territory would involve a discriminatory campaign of persecution. The intention to separate the ethnic communities by force, which included the knowledge that forcible, permanent removal of non-Serbs from Serbian-claimed territories would include a discriminatory campaign of persecution is herein after referred to as the object of ethnic separation by force." And just the first sentence of the next paragraph: "In 1991 and the months following --" I'm sorry, "In October 1991 and the months following, the SDS intensified efforts to ensure that the objective of ethnic separation by force would be achieved in the event that a negotiated solution did not occur." Sir, were you aware of the SDS policy of ethnic separation by force?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of this. I only mentioned Cutilheiro's plan, which was adopted by the SDS. But if I know correctly, the HDZ and the SDA also accepted the Cutilheiro plan, which related to the separation or cantonisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me that Biljana Plavsic, one of the three leaders of the SDS party, who was working closely with Radovan Karadzic and Momcilo Krajisnik, was better informed about SDS policies than you were in Bosanski Samac at the time?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: It is perfectly logical that a president or member of the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina has a better knowledge than just a regular member of the Municipal Assembly who at the time was a student, such as myself, and I'm saying once again that I'm not aware of this at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Fine. Let's move on to another SDS leader, Radovan Karadzic. Were you aware that Mr. Radovan Karadzic spoke at the 16th assembly of the people of the Republika Srpska, which was held on May 12th, 1992, and he spoke about the strategic goal of ethnic separation, and he made a very short statement: "The Serbian side in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the presidency, the government, the council for national security, which we've set up, have formulated strategic priorities, that is to say, strategic goals for the Serbian people. The first such goal is the separation from the other two national communities, separation of states, separation from those who are our enemies and who have used every opportunity, especially in this century, to attack us and who would continue with such practices if we were to continue to stay together in the same state." Were you aware of Mr. Karadzic's statement concerning ethnic separation at that People's Assembly?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: You're mentioning the 16th of May. In the month of May in 1992, I was in my unit, on the front line. I was taking care of the wounded. When I got home, we had no electricity, no water. I lived in abnormal conditions. How did you want me to get this type of information? I wasn't even reading the media, I wasn't reading the newspapers, because that wasn't in existence. And this is quite new to me. I was not able to get information at that time. We got no information, and I didn't have any opportunity to see this or to hear it anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware - maybe you learned this later - a written decision was issued as a result of that meeting by another SDS leader, Momcilo Krajisnik, which was signed on the 12th of May, 1992. It was a decision on strategic objectives of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, with the first objective being the separation of the Serbian people from the other two ethnic communities. A copy of that is an exhibit in this case. Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's take a step back. Again we'll go back to Mr. Karadzic, to February 25th, 1992, to the eight session of the assembly of the Serbian people. And at that time, Karadzic warns: "Once the party has adopted a policy, anything else is treason. Anything outside the adopted policy is treason. Assisting the enemy cannot be tolerated, giving him a way out and confusing the people while being a member of that party of the assembly and the party organs. That cannot be. I will not allow it. I will signal to the people: People, this man is a traitor. That is what I will do in the future." Were you aware of Karadzic's statement that anyone who violates party policy or disagrees or takes actions outside of party policy will be deemed a traitor? Were you aware of that statement by Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that statement by Mr. Karadzic. But in the world it is customary that if somebody is not in agreement with policies and the programme of a certain party, that such a person would be sanctioned or would be excluded from such a political party, and really, this is the first time I hear such a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, since we've heard -- I'm sorry. Let me take that back. Sir, since the non-Serb population of Bosanski Samac had practically disappeared, and this all occurred after this SDS policy of ethnic separation, which was just discussed here, by Karadzic, Krajisnik, and Plavsic, would you agree with me, sir, that the policy of those SDS leaders was implemented in Samac?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I do not understand your question. What do you mean by that? Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I've just told you, and I've quoted statements from the SDS leaders of a policy of ethnic separation, and right after that policy is established, the non-Serb population of Samac practically disappears from the community of Samac, just as envisioned in that policy. Would you agree, since we know that to be a fact, would you agree, sir, that that policy was implemented in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection, objection, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Why, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. First of all, could my learned friend explain to this witness: What is the term "disappeared"? Physical sense or in a spiritual sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic. That is clear. There's no reason why he should explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Especially, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There is nothing wrong with the question. Let the proceedings go on, Mr. Pantelic. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I do not understand what you mean by "disappeared." Because in the former territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac, one part of the population created the municipality of Bosanski Samac. Croats live on that territory. And we are talking about Domaljevac, Bazik, the territory around Grebnice, Prud. And here we are talking about a majority of the Croatian population. Another part of the Croatian population spent the whole war in Samac and some other Muslims also were members of the army of the Republika Srpska, and they still live to this date on those territories. It is true that I have heard that some people detained a certain amount of people and the police detained them because they had found weapons in their houses. But there was a very small difference now with regards to voters in respect to the pre-war period. But during the war, there was a migration, Croatian migration, Serbian migration, and people were living in a state of psychosis and they were bringing their families to Serbia, to Croatia, they were leaving the territory. And I must say that during the war some several hundreds of Serbs also left because they were afraid of the multi-ethnic war, and so some people brought their families in Croatia, the people in Serbia. So this psychosis that existed in the pre-war period existed also during the war and it is just something that was felt in the air. And this is why there was a natural migration of people going in different places, and in fact because of the fear, people were leaving, Serbs were leaving, Croats were leaving, and the Muslims were leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So sir, it's your opinion that this is nothing more than a coincidence that there is a change in the population after the policy, the SDS policy to separate the ethnic communities was established, and after the Serbs seized power? It's nothing more than some sort of a coincidence that there was a policy to separate the ethnic groups and that the population, a certain amount of the population of the non-Serb community is no longer in Samac?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: The plans and the goals of the SDS were never tied to any discriminatory policies on the basis of ethnic discrimination. As far as I know, in Samac, before the war and during the war, as well as after the war, Serbs, Croats, and Muslims lived together. And even today you have a policy through which hundreds of thousands of people [as interpreted] have left the municipality of Samac because just people wanted to go and find a better living. It is perfectly normal that everybody tries to flee an area which is being under attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... here on page 63, line 20, where it says: "Policy through which hundreds of thousands of people have left the municipality." Obviously the witness said hundreds of people, not hundreds of thousands. Before the war, there were not even 100.000 people at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And I do apologise to my learned friend and to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: First of all, the correction by Mr. Lazarevic is accepted. Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much. Intervention to the transcript. It's page 63, line 22 and 23. This witness, Dr. Pivasevic, very clearly said that the -- it's perfectly normal that everybody tries to flee an area during the wartime period. Dr. Pivasevic didn't say that this part of sentence which is, I'm quoting, on line 21: "Which is being under attack." It's a very big difference. So it's just a correction in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think Mr. Weiner can deal with that with the witness, as to what he exactly said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, was your statement that people leave -- will flee an area which is being under attack? Did you say during a wartime period, people will flee an area during a wartime period? Was that your statement to the court?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I don't quite know how it was interpreted, but I said very clearly: An area that's devastated by war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But sir, were you aware that there was an exchange process, and over 1.000 people left Bosanski Samac through an exchange process?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I did hear about the exchanges, but I don't know anything specific. I don't know any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you indicated at one point that it had nothing to do with any SDS policy, because there was no SDS discriminatory policy, but you also will agree with me, sir, that of the three major SDS leaders - Plavsic, Krajisnik, and Karadzic, one has pled guilty to persecution, one is going on trial for genocide and a third one is a fugitive from justice? Isn't that correct? Fugitive from justice being charged with war crimes?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I said about Mrs. Plavsic that every statement she made and her plea are her own personal business. I have already answered this question. What Mrs. Plavsic said need not be correct. As for the other two people from the SDS, they are only indicted. As far as I know, to be indicted does not mean to be guilty necessarily. I'm no legal expert, but as far as I know, they have not been convicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you also know that Mr. Karadzic is a fugitive from justice, he hasn't turned himself in to stand trial, he's wanted for war crimes? As the whole world knows that he's wanted.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I know from the media that Dr. Karadzic has been indicted and that he has not surrendered. Had he done so, the media would most probably have reported about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you indicated that there was no relationship between the JNA, the Yugoslavian National Army and the SDS. Once again, were you aware that Biljana Plavsic as part of her plea has discussed the relationship between the JNA and the SDS and indicated that the SDS collaborated with the JNA to arm members of the SDS and arm the Serbian population of Bosnia? Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I was not aware of that. I knew that the policy of the SDS, ever since its founding, was to advocate the preservation of Yugoslavia as a federal community and to support the JNA, as the only legitimate armed force on the territory of the former Yugoslavia. This was the policy from the beginning, from the founding of the SDS. The struggle to preserve a federal Yugoslavia. Of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question is: Were you aware of Biljana Plavsic's admission that the SDS collaborated with the JNA in arming large segments of the Bosnian population? Were you aware of that? It could be yes, it could be no.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No. I have to admit that I did not follow the trial of Mrs. Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let us move on. Do you know who Milan Simic is? He was a defendant in this case. Do you know who he was, from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know Milan Simic. But I only got to know him in 1994 or 1995, I think. I heard that he was the president of the Executive Board, but I did not know Mr. Milan Simic at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And sir, were you aware that he has pled guilty in this case to torturing five non-Serbs in the primary school in Samac? He's pled guilty to that. Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I did hear some details in town, talking to people, but, to be quite honest, what he pled guilty to, I don't know. I don't follow trials from The Hague very closely, because I have other obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware that as part of his plea to the 4th amended indictment, he admitted to paragraph 30, and that's according to the sentencing judgement, on page 5, he's admitted to paragraph 30, which states: "Bosnia and Herzegovina declared its independence from Yugoslavia on 29 February 1992. Long before this, however, the SDS and the JNA had been making plans for the probability of a war, which included the creation of separate Serb-controlled municipalities throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina." Were you aware of Milan Simic's admission in relation to the SDS and the JNA?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about the admission of Mr. Simic, but the date that you mentioned was the date of the referendum of the other two constituent peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is, the Muslims and Croats, about the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I think that somebody from the European structures put this as a precondition, that a referendum had to be held and that a two-thirds majority had to be obtained in order for Bosnia and Herzegovina to be recognised. In my view, this referendum was not legitimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: My question doesn't regard the legitimacy of the referendum. That's up to the badinter commission. My question is: Were you aware that Milan Simic has admitted complicity between the JNA and the SDS that they were making plans -- let me read the statement again: "Milan Simic has admitted that the SDS and the JNA had been making plans for the probability of a war, which included the creation of separate Serb-controlled municipalities throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina." Are you aware that the former president of the Executive Board of the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac made that statement?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that. As I said, because of my obligations, I do not follow the trials here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Were you aware, sir, or have you ever heard of Major General Milan Gvero, commander of the 1st Krajina Corps, and were you aware that on September 23rd, 1993, he addressed the People's Assembly of the Republika Srpska and he credited the SDS for working with the JNA and others to arm the Serbian people of Bosnia? Were you aware of the Major General's statement to the People's Assembly of the Republika Srpska? That's the 34th session.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I have heard of General Gvero, but I did not follow the proceedings of the assembly at that time, for various reasons. And I'm not aware of this statement. In that period of time, I was not active in political life. I spent that time studying, and I spent most of my time in Belgrade, taking exams. And if I did read the newspapers from time to time, 11 years later, after all those exams and after doing my specialist training, I am not able to remember these statements made by various generals and politicians. Even today the newspapers are full of statements made by various people, but one can't remember them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But would you agree with me, sir, that the Major General was in a far better position than yourself to discuss the work of the JNA and the SDS?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I agree that he was in a far better position, that he was better informed, and I don't know what he meant by this. I would have to see the entire text of his statement in order to make some sort of judgement about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you know who Simo Zaric is, a defendant in this case?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I met Mr. Zaric as a boy, because Mr. Zaric played football, or rather, soccer, together with my father, in a soccer team where my father played. He was a sports worker. And I knew him as a man who was interested in folklore, in matters characteristic for our local community. I once treated his mother-in-law, and I think he once brought his son to me for a check-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, were you aware that Mr. Zaric was an intelligence officer in the 4th Detachment and for years had been involved in intelligence, working for state security?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, I would see Mr. Zaric in a soldier's uniform during the war, but what he actually did in specific terms, I couldn't tell you. There were many soldiers around. Each one had his own tasks. So I couldn't go into those details.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Zaric has provided a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, and in that statement, which is P140 ter, at 28 to 30, at pages 28 to 30, he has stated to an investigator or actually to some prosecutors that the SDS was illegally arming its members. Were you aware of that, sir, that Mr. Zaric has given a statement indicating that the SDS was illegally arming its own members?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I've already repeated several times that because of my medical duties, I do not follow the trials in the Hague, and I simply am not aware of these statements. I'm not referring just to this trial, but any trial here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, since you know Mr. Zaric, are you aware of any reason why Mr. Zaric would lie about a statement that the SDS in Samac was illegally arming its members? Are you aware of any reason which would cause him to lie about that?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I really can't go into something that I personally have not heard. It would not be proper for me to say anything about statements made by other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. Do you know a man by the name of Mico Ivanovic, who was a board member of the SDS in Samac?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know Mr. Ivanovic and I know he was one of the people in the steering committee for the establishment of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In fact, he was on the SDS party ticket in 1990 and was elected to the assembly in that same year; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: He could only have been elected an assemblyman, not a deputy. A deputy is a member of the republican parliament. So that Mirko Jovanovic could only have been elected to the local parliament. I don't remember how many members we had exactly, but we were the largest political party along with the HDZ [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I'm -- excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. His answer is absolutely not correctly translated, so I ask my learned friend and the witness to actually witness to repeat slowly his answer. Because it is page 70, line 17 and 21. It's a mess. Mirko Jovanovic for the local parliament. He spoke that Mirko Jovanovic was for the republic parliament of B and H. So it is a complete mess. So I kindly ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I can fix it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir isn't it true that Mirko Jovanovic was elected to the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac in 1990, the Municipal Assembly, not the regional or national level, Mico Ivanovic?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I allow for that possibility that he was elected to the local assembly. I don't know the names of all the people who were elected and who became members of the local assembly, because I never attended any of their sessions. There is a municipal Official Gazette listing the people elected to the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. And it's in evidence here at P8 and his name is on it as being elected.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's time for a break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We shall take our break now and continue at 1805.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Winding up?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I had about another 20 minutes to go, Your Honour. I'll try and move it fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning -- I'm sorry. Good afternoon, Dr. Pivasevic. When we left we were talking about Mico Ivanovic, who was a member of the steering committee of the SDS. Were you aware that as commander of the 1st Detachment, he and Stevan Todorovic met the paramilitaries or the Serbian volunteers when they arrived in Batkusa on JNA helicopters? Were you aware of that SDS leader being there with Stevan Todorovic to meet them?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Mico Ivanovic was a member of the Municipal Assembly. I do not know who or where met those people, or rather the Municipal Board.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter corrects herself.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know who met those people, or where, and I don't know whether Dr. Simic was there or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, on the following day, after their arrival, the defendant Blagoje Simic, the SDS president, and Mirko Jovanovic, who -- an SDS member who you later said became a deputy to parliament, or a representative to parliament, met with the paramilitary leaders on or about April 12, 1992. Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise to my learned friend. Please, what exactly my learned friend want to make reference, that Mirko Jovanovic was a deputy or a representative? Because these are two different terms. So please be precise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mirko Jovanovic, who you indicated was a -- later became -- I believe you used the term a representative to parliament or did you use the term "a deputy to parliament"?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Mirko Jovanovic became a deputy in the republican assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, while Mico Ivanovic was an assemblyman in the Municipal Assembly of Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So on the following day, on or about April 12th, were you aware that on or about April 12th, 1992, the SDS president, Blagoje Simic, and Mirko Jovanovic, an SDS member and later deputy in the republican assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina, met with the paramilitary leaders? Were you aware of that? There's been testimony about that in this case.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know this. I don't know what happened on 12th April last month, let alone so many years ago. I don't know. I didn't hear anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Sir, having heard this information, the information from Biljana Plavsic about the relationship between the JNA and the SDS, similar testimony or similar statements from Major General Gvero, the statement of Milan Simic about SDS and JNA plans, the testimony -- the statement of Simo Zaric relating to arming of SDS members, do you wish to change your testimony that the SDS had no ties to the JNA, after hearing all those quotes?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the SDS did not have any ties with the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: As far as you know, strictly based on your knowledge, personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, there was some discussion concerning some local men that were sent to training, paramilitary training, and it said Serbia, but I believe the town was Ilok, which is in the Serbian Krajina of Croatia; is that correct? Ilok is in Serbian Krajina? Were you aware that some local men were sent for training to Ilok?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I have heard about Ilok. It was in Croatia, yes, in the Serbian Krajina. And as for men being sent for training in Ilok, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man by the name of Aco Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The name is familiar to me. He's the son of a man whom I'm treating.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, were you aware that Aco Jankovic is related to the Simic family, that he's a relative of Milan Simic's wife? If you're aware. Yes, no. Are you aware that Aco Jankovic is related to the Simic family?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of it. I know that Milan's wife, whom I met later through Milan's mother, who is coming to me for treatment, that a daughter of this uncle Pero Jankovic is related to Aco.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that Aco Jankovic led the local men to Ilok for training? Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I'm really not aware of this. These are military matters, training and such things are outside my domain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it fair to say that you weren't present for any conversations between Blagoje Simic and Aco Jankovic, Milos Bogdanovic, Stevan Todorovic, or any JNA leaders? Were you present for all conversations between Blagoje Simic and those persons?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: How could I have been present? Blagoje Simic was the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly, and I had no post at that time. I did not accompany him and go around with him so that I might be able to hear who he was meeting and what they were talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So sir, if you weren't present for any of the defendant Blagoje Simic's conversations between those people, you can't tell us what, if any, conversations he had in relation to persons being sent to Ilok?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection. Calling for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's obvious if he wasn't present for the conversations, he can't state what occurred in them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Basically, sir, if you weren't present for any of those conversations, you cannot tell us what, if any, conversation, or what, if any, discussion they had relating to persons being sent to Ilok?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I told you: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, earlier today you were shown a document which we referred to as the variant A and B document, which concerns certain directions that the municipalities are to take, and you indicated that you saw that document, which we called P3, this is a similar document, P145A, that you saw that document for the first time when it was handed to you. Is that correct? Did you see that document for the first time an hour and a half ago today?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. I saw it an hour and a half ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you never had the opportunity to study that document and read each and every paragraph of it, or in those few seconds were you able to read each and every paragraph and sentence of that document?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: In essence, I glanced through the document and I saw the topics written about in this document, and I know that I never read anything about such topics, which is why I said that this was the first time I had seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, again, sir, were you aware that this was a secret document sent to local municipal leaders, certain local municipal leaders, by the SDS leadership?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the document, so of course I cannot know whether it is confidential or public, the document itself is not familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware that Biljana Plavsic, as part of the factual basis for her plea, has stated that the SDS issued certain instructions to SDS municipal leaders and the municipal staffs implemented those directives? That's paragraph 12 of P164. Were you aware that she made that statement?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it. The only document I know about is the Official Gazette. I think from February 1992, where the assembly of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was established in January, said something about the establishment of Serbian assemblies. It is well known that the Serbian assembly was actually a response to the violation of the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina, where one of the constituent peoples was outvoted. I don't consider that the document published in an Official Gazette is a secret or illegitimate document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, then let's go to that January assembly. That's the sixth session, the assembly of the Serbian people of the 26th of January, 1992. At that assembly, a delegate named Cizmovic declared that the tasks set in the instructions of 19 December 1991, the tasks set in the instructions of 19 December 1991 should be carried out. And as we all know, the variant A and B document was dated 19 December 1991 and it was a set of directives and instructions. Were you aware of that statement being made at the sixth session of the assembly of the Serbian people by a delegate?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know Mr. Cizmovic, and I really don't remember following this session in January 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, would you agree with me that since you were tied up -- since you were involved in medical school, you were getting ready to go to the army, you were involved in local politics in Bosanski Samac, that there were a lot of things, because you were so busy, there were a lot of things or a lot of acts and activities of the SDS that were occurring that you don't know about? You're not aware of all of the different assembly statements and speeches. Would you agree that there were a lot of activities that occurred among the SDS leaders and members that you just don't have any knowledge of?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: It's very difficult to answer a question as to what happened somewhere where I was not. I really cannot give you a valid answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, let's go to Bosanski Samac. We know that a Serbian assembly was convened and proclaimed in late February of 1992. Were you aware that that was required under variant A and B, under paragraph 4 of variant A and B, that a Serbian assembly should be convened and proclaimed? Were you aware of that when you quickly looked at the variant A and B document? I think you said you glanced at the document. Were you aware that that was a requirement?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, I can, sir. Were you aware that that was a requirement, that a Serbian assembly should be convened and proclaimed in the -- it was required by the variant A and B document?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Variant A and B, I don't know anything about that. I heard that the Serb municipality had been set up, Samac and Pelagicevo, and that it has been established by a legitimate assemblymen. I was not present, because I was not in the town itself. I wasn't communicating to people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Another quick question: You said it was established by legitimate assemblymen. The assembly in that Samac assembly was composed of SDS officials and Serbian municipal leaders. Were you aware that that was required by the variant A and B document, variant B, paragraph 14 -- paragraph 4, I'm sorry. Were you aware that that was a requirement, SDS officials and Serbian municipal leaders would become members of the assembly?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I told you that it was only once in my life when I became a deputy and the assembly of Republika Srpska, I was only present at one session of the local assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I have several others to ask you. At that first assembly meeting Ilija Ristic was elected president of the Serbian municipality of Samac. He was elected at the first meeting. Were you aware that the election of president at the first meeting of the Municipal Assembly was required by variant B, by the variant A and B document? You can say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say yes or no because the question has been asked like that. I cannot answer with a yes or no. I heard that Mr. Ristic had been elected as the president of the Serbian assembly. And as far as variants A and B, I'm telling you for the umpteenth time, this is the first time today that I saw some instructions of what you call variant A and B. So I cannot answer this question. I cannot answer with a yes or no regarding something I don't know anything about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You can also answer with I don't know which is fine. Sir, plans were made for the formation of a Serbian municipal government including composition and powers of the assembly, the election of municipal officials, election and voting plans. Those were all made at that first meeting. Were you aware that such activity was required by the variant A and B document, paragraph 5, by variant -- of variant B? You can say yes, you can say no, or you can say I don't know?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Another meeting was held of that Serbian assembly in March of 1992, where a municipal Executive Board and other municipal officials were appointed. And you'll notice that on page 12 in the -- in Exhibit P124. And which is the Official Gazette. Now, sir, did you know that the election of Executive Board members and other municipal officials or the appointment of Executive Board members and other municipal officials was required by variant -- by the variant A and B document, variant B, second phase, paragraph 1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. Maybe if there is some reference to certain exhibit maybe it would be fair for the witness to have this particular evidence in front of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He could have P124 and P3 or 145A. They're both the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If you go to page 12 in Exhibit 124. In the B/C/S, it should be decision on the election of members of the Executive Council, Article 1, and it's the first article under 28 March 1992. Eleven persons were elected to the Executive Board. Were you aware that such action was required under the variant A and B document, B, second phase of variant B, second one?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that the Executive Board was elected or their content. It was impossible for me to read this report, because when it was issued, I was in Brcko, working as a -- following the ending of my medical school, working as a junior doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we further look at those persons elected, a police chief, and as two deputies, as well as a TO chief, a Territorial Defence chief, were appointed at that meeting, in that same list. Were you aware that this was required under variant B, paragraph 8?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know anything about that document, variant A, variant B, so I don't -- I can't know this either, theoretically. There is no possibility that I would be able to know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll just do a few more, sir. A Crisis Staff was established in Samac in April of 1992. The president of the SDS was named president of that Crisis Staff. Were you aware that both of those were requirements under variant A and B document, the establishment of a Crisis Staff and that the SDS president must be the Crisis Staff president? Were you aware of both of those directives under the variant A and B document?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Several days after the war clashes started, I found out that Dr. Simic was the president of the Crisis Staff. I also found out that Simeun Simic was of the executive as well as Savo Popovic. These were the people that I knew. There was a paper which was like a bulletin or a newsletter that was published and this was done by Mr. Simic. I mean by Mr. Simeun.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you also aware that the defendant Blagoje Simic was named president of the assembly at the initiative of the SDS board, that the SDS municipal board, and that is stated right here in the municipal gazette, page 21. Were you aware of that, that the SDS municipal board came up with the initiative that he should become president?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean regarding the president of the Crisis Staff? Could you please repeat the question. I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: According to the Official Gazette of Bosanski Samac, or the Serbian municipality of Samac, it indicates that the defendant Blagoje Simic was named president of the assembly at the initiative of the SDS municipal board. Were you aware of that? And that's on page 21, conclusions of April 14th, 1992, conclusion number 5.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know anything about this. I know that Blagoje was the vice-president of the assembly following the party elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Finally, sir: Orders were issued to the police chief, to immediately establish a special police unit that will work with military and civilian authorities. Were you aware that those orders given to the police chief were required by the variant A and B document in phase 1 of the document, paragraphs 5 and 8, and in phase 2 of the document, paragraph 2? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to read you one final quotation and finish today. It's a statement at that same May 12th, 1992 session of the People's Assembly of the Republika Srpska, and it's from Miroslav Vjestica and I left this one for last because he was named as an appointment in Bosanska Krupa, pursuant to variant A and you probably know him because he was deputy prime minister for internal affairs army, police and justice. He was deputy president of the RS assembly. Do you know who I'm talking about, sir?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Vjestica, during the first assembly of the People's Assembly, after the Dayton Agreement, he was the vice-president of the People's Assembly. He was the deputy of Mr. Dragan Kalinic. But what this is about, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, at that same meeting where the first objective of separating the ethnicities was discussed and agreed upon, he got up and said: "On the right bank of the Una River there are no more Muslims in the Serbian municipality of Bosanska Krupa. All of the enclaves that were there, Rapusa, Veliki Vrbovik, Ostroznica, Babic, Muslim Jasenica and Zavir, we have evacuated them so that there will be none there for the duration of the war operations. Will they have a place to return to? I think it is unlikely after our president told us the happy news that the right bank of the Una was the border." Were you aware of this quote by Mr. Vjestica, where he spoke happily about the removal of all Muslims from the area of Bosanska Krupa, and this was at the Republika Srpska assembly on May 12th, 1992, and this was the president of Bosanska Krupa SDS Municipal Board who, under variant B, became a member of the municipality of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that, for the simple reason that I've explained to you: We were not able to watch television at the time. There was no electricity. There were war clashes. I don't know where I was then, on the 12th. To tell you the truth, I didn't know even that the assembly was having a session then. There was no way or a mechanism for me to find out about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No further questions, sir. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Pivasevic, could you please have a look at this second document, this variant A and B, if you have it in front of you.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have in front of you just the Official Gazette or do you also have the other document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I just have the Official Gazette in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... P145 or P3. It's the same document, basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: 145A or P3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: 145A, yes. Thank you. Thank you, my friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, the Prosecutor asked you about the weapons and all the theories that he's developing. Can you tell me: Do you have any knowledge that the JNA had distributed weapons in the period before the middle of April 1992 in the town of Samac itself to the members of the -- to Muslims and Croats and Serbs through all various instances, specifically the 4th Detachment? Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I don't have any knowledge about that, because the JNA asked people to mobilise themselves. They were called for -- there was a call for mobilisation [Realtime transcript read in error "mobile scomblaigs"] predominantly of the Serbs but also of Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Where you fought, did you have fellow soldiers who were also Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean in the same unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: In the unit itself where I was, no, but in the larger formation, in the unit, in the battalion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Some small clarification of the answer that was given by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On page 84 line 12 and 13 there was a call obviously for mobilisation predominantly of the Serbs but also of Muslims and Croats. The witness said that there was a general call for mobilisation and the response was most by Serbs but also -- and I believe that this significantly changes the meaning of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe the witness can repeat his answer so that it's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Dr. Pivasevic, just slowly, could you repeat your answer to my question. My question -- just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mobilisation by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So my question was in relation to the 4th Detachment itself, as a part of the JNA, and I asked you whether you had any knowledge that members of the 4th Detachment, Serbs, Muslims, Croats, on the basis of a call for mobilisation, were issued with weapons. Now, could you please give a slow answer to that question again.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I was formationally not a member of the 4th Detachment, but when the war started, I saw that, because we were relatively near each other on the positions in that detachment there were Muslims, Croats and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I haven't heard anyone going to the combat position at the front line without any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So I conclude that they were armed. You agree with me?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the third or the fourth day of war, when I saw these units of the 4th Detachment that were there somewhere in the direction of Grebnice. They were next to us on the front line, on the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please look at a document that you were asked about by the Prosecutor, the alleged document. I don't know how to call it. We spent a lot of time here regarding this document. Could you please read the title of this document?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: "Instructions for the organisation activity of organs of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina in extraordinary circumstances Sarajevo 19th of December, 1991."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please turn to the last page of the document. What does it say there?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: It's very difficult to read, but at the end it says the Crisis Staff of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is there a seal?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: There's no seal and there is no signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You personally, did you have any knowledge about a body? Because we're speaking about the Main Board. The top of the party, did you ever hear, ever since you became a member of the SDS, that there was a Crisis Staff of the SDS on the level of the Main Board of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I became a member of the Main Board in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Slow down. Slow down, please. Dr. Pivasevic, it's a very simple question. Let's not expand on that. We don't have much time. From 1998 until you became -- 1990, when you became a member of the SDS, did you ever hear that there was such a body, Crisis Staff of the SDS at the level of the Main Board of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please carefully look at the Official Gazette which is in front of you. Look at each page and tell us whether anywhere, in any part of that document, the Official Gazette, you have this title that you have just read of this document, the variant A and B document, which is instructions for the organisation and activity, et cetera, et cetera. Could you please have a look at the entire Official Gazette and tell me if anywhere there is any decision which is referring to this document.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, this title is not to be found anywhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Further on, could you please describe to the Trial Chamber, when any act is coming from the Main Board of the SDS to the Municipal Board, do you receive papers, instructions, documents, without a seal, without a signature, without a reference, a log number, in your experience?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: From 1990, when -- since I've been a member, I haven't seen such an occurrence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: While you were a member of the Municipal Board, in the period from 1990 onwards, did you ever see a document, an SDS document, coming from above, that -- coming to the Municipal Board without a seal, without a signature, and so on? Have you ever personally seen such a document?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I very rarely have seen any documents, but particularly any documents without a seal and signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you a question with regard to that Cizmovic. Did you know that he was a deputy of the SPO at the time? You have heard of that I presume.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Well, to tell you honestly --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just answer with a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please tell us: With regard to the discussion relating to Cutilheiro plan and Lisbon Agreement --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the rest of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will repeat the question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question was the following: Did the SDS, after the Lisbon Agreement, support all the peaceful international plans, including the Dayton Agreement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Number one, it's very leading. Number two, I did not raise the Lisbon agreement or the Cutilheiro plan. However, he did mention it, and if you remember, I stopped him in mid-sentence or midstream, when he started to go on about this, because it was not in response to any question which I raised. And it's also number 3, it's outside, because I didn't raise anything about international plans, including the Dayton Agreement, which is beyond the jurisdiction of this indictment. Dayton plan 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, my learned friend actually asked this witness with regard to the position of SDS, of the policy of SDS, so the part of my clarification of the policy of SDS is also peace initiatives and activities of SDS. According to the personal knowledge of this witness. Because he said "policy." Were you aware of the policies? There are many meanings of policies. I'm referring to peace policies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If that is the question, then that's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is the question, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then that is different from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- elaborate my position as Defence counsel as Defence for Dr. Blagoje Simic, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Because that was different from the question to which Mr. Weiner had objected. He's now only asking the witness as to the policies of the SDS with regard to peace initiatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's fair. I'll withdraw, as long as it's not leading and it's a general question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very briefly, Dr. Pivasevic: Do you know what the SDS did after -- or what were the activities of the SDS with regard to the Lisbon Agreement and the Cutilheiro plan?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They adopted the Cutilheiro plan, and I also know that the SDS at the time did not take part of the forums of the SDS but through the media I also know that they had a certain position taken with regard to the Dayton Agreement and it was adopted [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in the end, it is not my last question. I do have a few more questions for you. But my learned friend Mr. Weiner asked you a question about General Gvero. He even quoted to you, or actually, he related to you his words. Do you know if General Gvero was a member of the SKPU, that party. It's the League of the Communist Movement for Yugoslavia. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know, are you aware of the fact that that party was not very favourable with regard to the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Pivasevic, are you aware of the fact that at the head of this party was Mrs. Mira Markovic, and that the Main Board was made by the generals of the JNA? Do you know? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Exactly who is testifying at this point. I object.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. I will rephrase. I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, what is your personal knowledge of the -- of who was in the presidency of the League of the Communists for the Movement of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I have heard about General Mirkovic, who was a general and he was retired at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Mira Markovic was there as well?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: I really can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: As a matter of clarification, Mira Markovic or Mrs. Mira Markovic, is that the wife of Slobodan Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I just want to ask maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Pivasevic, Mira Markovic was -- or is she the wife of Mr. Slobodan Milosevic? Do you know that fact? Yes or no. I'm just asking you if Mrs. Mira Markovic is the wife of Mr. Milosevic. Listen to me. Do not look at the screen?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that Mrs. Mira Markovic is the wife of Mr. Slobodan Milosevic and that she was the president of the Jul in Serbia. She was the director, if you will. She was at the head of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you know that that party had a name SK [phoen] movement for Yugoslavia before that?

utterances.speaker: STANKO PIVASEVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm really not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I've finished with the examination of this witness. [Interpretation] Thank you, Dr. Pivasevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Anybody wishes to ask the witness questions? No?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Pivasevic. We are finished with you. You may leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now and continue our proceedings tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of May 2003, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.53 p.m.,
